Inflation, rising costs, labor shortages, and new waves of bias and xenophobia continue to test us. Our community faces obstacles that go beyond the economy, ones rooted in perception, misunderstanding, and sometimes unequal access to opportunity. We are also navigating a climate where immigrants and immigrant families, many within our AANHPI community, are often treated with suspicion, dismissed, or even targeted. In times like these, it's important to remind everyone here. Many of us, through grandparents or parents, came here out of courage. We came here to work hard and build a life, and we chose Lancaster as our home. public_comments.text: uh tonight i'd like to take a moment to recognize the school district of lancaster and its incredible students over the years sdol and the city have built a strong and meaningful partnership and i want to recognize a few pieces of sdl news so first i want to congratulate mccaskey's unified track and field and varsity track and field athletes athletes who competed at the pi double a state championships at shippensburg this past weekend varsity track and field team place second and remarkable achievement and all the student athletes make our entire city proud and the only reason why I had awareness of this is that last week I and several city staff had the pleasure of judging the school district of Lancaster STEM fair and it was as I was leaving the STEM fair that there was the drumline and all the cheerleaders as they were sending off the athletes on onto the bus to head to Shippensburg. And it was just such a wonderful moment of school spirit and community pride. So I just wanna recognize that. And then as it relates to the STEM fair, several of us had the chance to go and judge projects. And I think as well, Councilor Arroyo, Molly, our Deputy Director of Public Works for Sustainability, Rebecca, who you heard from tonight, and Betsy, also who you heard from tonight, got to witness the passion and innovation of these young minds at the STEM Fair, and their projects were pretty amazing. And they have recently taken on a number of projects that are directly related to the city, whether that's around stormwater or litter. And I just, I highly recommend if council members ever get asked to go to absolutely do it, because you will be shocked what these kids are coming up with I also you know one of the key programs connecting the city and the school district has been the JP McCaskey neighborhood leaders Academy which has been an outstanding program over the years with 84 students compete completing it since its inception at our last meeting we saw this and the program continues to shape future leaders and strengthen the ties between McCaskey and our city government and just this morning I attended the witness stones project ceremony and saw the hard work of McCaskey social studies students who researched the stories of four enslaved residents of Lancaster they spoke eloquently at the ceremony about the research that they did and what they learned about these four individuals one two of them were children and it was really clear that they were passionate about the project and finally this week is McCaskey's graduation it will be held on thursday night an annual highlight for sure i have the opportunity to speak at the ceremony and to celebrate their perseverance and dedication and this one this last one will certainly be extra special for me to celebrate the class of 2025. so i'm really deeply proud of how our city employees have embraced collaboration with the school district on key initiatives like bike and and pedestrian safety youth engagement public safety and community building there is much more to collaborate on and I'm grateful both to our city departments and school district of Lancaster staff who are really eager to keep that partnership going strong thank you council thank you very much mayor
